display.title: Serving Hashem with Joy: Why Rabbi Levi Yitzchak Skipped a Blessing
display.summary_short: Where does real happiness come from? Uncle Yossi answers with the story of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev, who was so happy to be a Jew that he could not wait to say the brachah.
display.summary_long: A talk on simchah from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi quotes Dovid HaMelech, 'Serve Hashem with joy', and asks where real happiness comes from, since no one can just push a button and be happy. He tells a true story of Rabbi Levi Yitzchak of Berditchev. Honored to lead the morning brachos in shul, the tzaddik skipped the blessing thanking Hashem for making us Jewish, and the congregation waited respectfully until after davening to ask why. He explained that while saying Modeh Ani in bed he thought about who is speaking and before Whom: Hashem, the eternal King, had returned his Jewish neshamah, a part of Hashem Himself. Overjoyed, he washed negel vasser and said that brachah at once, out loud. Uncle Yossi concludes that knowing we have a Jewish soul is reason to be happy twenty-four hours a day, and that we will leave golus in joy when Moshiach comes. The clip ends as he introduces the march 'Ki B'simchah Seitzeu'.
display.lesson: Knowing that we are Jews, with a neshamah that is truly a part of Hashem, is reason enough to serve Hashem with joy all day long.

date.note: Date of episode 491, from which the clip is cut ('this coming Shabbos is Rosh Chodesh Elul', 1991). The same talk also aired in episode 138.
